.
Four letters  and several names.
Like to see what others might come up with or already came up with.
I guess this post is so burried and very few dare to click a link in a signature, that i can freely write what i "might" have found out (gotta scratch that itch).
And if someone reads this, i can watch the virus spread
Given all the cryptics we have in the game, ceasar zypher, hexdec, i guess binary was a thing and who knows what else, starting with amiokay i tried tho find more clues in names.
Maya Makinami seemed already to be a hint to something. In a theory where Maya might be Ami's true mother, with Sensei as the father, it would make sense that Maya (is/was) makin' Ami.
But i couldn't find any more names with a meaning, that is, until recently.
So is, for those who know, Amiokay just Am i Okay or Ami Okay?
I think it might be neither of those.
Maybe everything revoles around Maya - M A Y A.
I have i theory and i stated that way above in this post, that girls in Kumon'mi might be split apart or maybe copies of, either Senseis and or Maya's and who knows who else's mind.
So i started looking for Maya's and Sensei's in other girls and i think i found some (Maya's).
Most important and what made me think i might be right:
Yumi Yamaguchi.
As i said it's about M A Y A.
So: Yumi Guchi Maya. Or Maya Guchi.
While there might be also a translation for Maya in japenese (i guess it was something like love or maybe love interest) Guchi "could" be translated as complaining. And i guess that would be a good definition of Yumis character. Always complaining of how shitty her life is or how Sensei treats her.
That in the end, as a part of Maya would make her Maya's complaining side of her character.
But there are more.
Ayane Amamiya
Amamiya -> Only thing that came up yet -> I am Maya.
So is Ayane the real Maya? A girl we have yet to see (Melon vendor)?
Or is she another fragment, with the letters IAM/MIA/AMI/MAI to make sense?
Makoto Miyamura
Miyamura -> Miru or Muri Maya. Or other combinations.
So this is rather tough. Miru would be to look after someone, like medically caring. Or caring in general which "could" suit Makoto as she's always looking after Sensei to help him, as the class president. Maybe also in another way? A Maya that looked after Seinsei/Cared for him?
Muri seems to be generally about impossible things. Or meaning unreasonable. Makoto the unreasonable Maya? Don't know.
Miku Maruyama
Maruyama -> Maru or Mura Maya?  Whatever it is i can't come up with a meaningful answer. Village, circle, complete maybe someting i didn't find out yet.
My guess would be to find some word meaning unsteady, energetic or jittery.
Futaba Fukuyama
Fukuyama ->Fuku Maya? Fuku can mean happy among a ton of other things i guess (vice/clothes/happy). While kufu on ther other hand means things like fear, terror, horror and so on. Could make her, amongst others, the happy or scared Maya.
Noriko Nakayama
Nakayama -> Naka Maya? Naka describes something to be inside something else and to also be the centerpoint of something inside something else. It' can also mean middle and relationship.
Amiokay -> Koi Maya? Kio? Also a lot to find in the net about what that could mean. Center, lover, deep, this jerk ( Maya is a nerd?
) i think even Hope was something possible.
So my big problem here is that i am almost incabable of understanding the japanese language.
So if anyone good at japanese or native japanese ever finds this, please correct me.
In the end i could totally be wrong with everything, i know that. It's just about how Yumi's last name fit her discription. And how several girls of the original cast have a maya in their last names. Could be a coincidence of course.
And thats it for now. Took me way too long again.

spoilers.title: Warning: This is long
spoilers.html:
"In the beginning"
So as i think its already verified, Sensei has tried to kill himself (Confirmed by Sensei .14) and may or may not have suceeded (Lives, but is badly injured). Threw himself from a ("the school") rooftop (Maybe into the wishing well) (He made his choice). (A reference to that could be: "crumbling and liquifiying teeth" hitting the ground face forward)

"The car crash, or: Those who might have never existed at all"
So i guess this is very early on in the game.
I think it was Ami (with Sensei not remembering) saying that her parents died in a car crash. (Hello Kaori?Miku?)
We have that scene where Sensei and Ami are in front of a gravestone which has the names Sekai (sister in law) and Nozomu (brother) on it.
So alot of people give their offsping names that have a meaning in their language for example ita "Bella=Beatiful".
But what if those names have more meaning to them?
As far as google was capable to help me: (jp)Sekai = world and (jp)Nozomu (want;hope;wish).
What if those two words mean "hopefull/wishfull world" or something. Maybe together with "Something is burried underneath your feet" (The painful truth).
What if thats not the grave of Ami's parents at all but that of (im gonne say it) Mayas and Senseis stillborn child? Which meant the wishfull/hopefull world to them (regarding how broken they have always been?).
Final words: There are two Kumon'mi girls (besides Ami) i can imagine having been part of the car crash, Miku and Kaori. How, i have yet to find out. I hope you get why i think that.

"Hope (what i assume is aka "The machine God") approaches"
We dont know what non Kumon'mi (forgot exect spelling) realword is, where he lived before.
So for now im just assuming that the real world he lived in was kind of slightly technically advanced to ours.
And i assume it has medical machines cabable of treating brain damage and mental ailments. (This really is the centerpoint for a lot im going to theorize about).
This is where i think Hope comes into play. I havent figured it out totally. There are theories besides f95 which give the whole trinity religous thing more account. But iirc its stated somewhere ingame that a lot of the "happy scenes" where just an overload of metaphors and philosophy to explain the early stages of Sensei dealing with him being "new" to Kumon'mi (and the reason he got there) and what not, so i'll leave most of that out. It even feels like Hope was hostile in the early stages but became more "friendly" towards the end of chapter one. (There's some sentence somewhere that goes by "sacrifice (give) him yourself and anyone you love". For now i assume that might just mean: be honest/open to him (or maybe give me "all your pain"))

"The purpose of Hope"
OK, back to good ol Hope and what he/it might be.
Maybe Sensei lays in a hospital/recreation center and is attached to some machine (withwiresandwiresandwiresandwires) attached to him, which is capable of slowly but steadily repairing his brain damages. And not only that. What if Hope is even capable of "repairing" mental ailments? Forget about all of the savage shocking therapies of the 20th century. Hope knows best! ("Just sacrifice yourself and all that you love (Your secrets/pains) to me (him)".)
So i and Zane (dont know if zane changed his mind (but credits due) ) thought what if Hope (as something to heal peoples minds) does this by creating an atificial world (vr) and represents all of Senseis mental ailmants as persons to get along with? That would be where most if not all of the girls are coming from. And i think you can get where this is going.
Face all of your ailments/fears as persons. And because Sensei is a guy... Bonus, they are all girls. Hooray.
Finally: The whole Sensei is connected to some kind of machine is reinforced with all the "UserX tries to access terminal 23" and the ip, port and password thing.

"The Maya (Or: The culture that thought worlds gonna end 21/12/2012 or 12/21/2012
([Redacted] its DD</MM</YYYY) )"
Oh yeah... Im going to talk about THAT girl. Eveything number related is just you having arithmomania (23 (google) unless its some kind of reverse logic or whatever (right english term to be confirmed)).
"Maya"
If she was a real person i'd really would have wanted to hug her in the scarf scene (Damn music Selebus).
So i guess alot of us saw "baby finches". I assume consense is that Sensei and Maya where in a relationship sometime.
There's a lot going on in that scene and it has alot ambiguous stuff in it (Spiders? what for? Spiders = Curse?Kaori?).
The whole conversation with Sensei and Maya is really weird not only because of the [redectad] stuff but also the topics (Cave in your newborn head (might be important (will refer to later)) killing kittens (is Sensei carrying dead kittens in those boxes before resets for Maya as a sacrifice?), how some birds kill their babies because they're weak or daddy wants to fuck a bit sooner). But i guess unless proven wrong, thats the time where Sensei openly openly confesses to Maya. Like hey we've been fucking around for some time, i think i might have fallin in love with you. M: "Ok you know i dont like that kinda talk... but thank you...".

"Maya the broken one"
Ok back to Sensei's mind being broken down into pieces (disassembled by Hope, his ailments are girls in Kumon'mi).
What if for some reasons Maya (the real person) is "connected" to hope too? (Because car crash/injured. Sensei mentioning pulling scrap metal out of someones body somewhere).
And what if Hope is a machine (machine god) and knows no way around as to disassemble Mayas mind into fragments too (because thats his purpose)?
That would mean that at least some of the girls in Kumon'mi are representations of Maya's mind. (I tried to discern girls by eye color but i dont know if that makes sense... like everything greenish being part of Maya and stuff...)
But im certain to a degree that HexDec Amiokay is another represantation of Maya (AMIOKAY says: I remeber something - It's a green scarf - And the arms of the only person to have ever truly loved me (who gave a green scarf to whom? )). With the real one laying so sexually depicted in that vat (because of all the life supporting tubes and wires). This might even go for Kumon'mi Maya who might not be her all self => Maya stripped from her mental ailments (But shes a smart girl knowing her ways around). Maybe she underwent the same process as Sensei does. Only that she was strong enough to make it to a level where she remembers most if not all of her past life without getting reset or Hope just gave up on resetting her because he deems her broken beyond repair. This could have happened in a time when the simulation started and Sensei was failing and failing again.
Finally we have tha scene in iirc .14 where Sensei uses his superpowers to scan Maya... "likes melons, plays violin,... at the end "is broken beyond repair"". Yeah.. thats a tough nut. Could mean her body and/or her mind is broken beyond repair.

"Mayas reasons"
"And the arms of the only person to have ever truly loved me" (This is either Maya to Sensei or Sensei to Maya.. but im going with Maya to Sensei)
So... Maya and Sensei relationship. I assume that both of them went trough some hard personal experiences.
You know how this can go. Fall in love with your soulmate, the one who really understands you.
And oh noes... Sensei gets stripped from most of his memories... placed into girls or what ever... hes not the person Maya once knew. While the same could be applied to her, but we'll see.
It is said that whenever Sensei learns to much at once about his past life he not only glitches but in the end either kills himself again (because he cannot handle the truth) and gets reset (by hope) or becomes insane and gets reset (by hope).
Maya insinuates that this has happened alot in the past.
What a dilemma. Does she hate Sensei for not being his former self? Is she trying to keep him at bay so he wont become his former self and resets everything (himself)? She feeds him bits of the truth here and there, so i guess she wants to guide him to a position where he can be as much as his former self without a reset.

"Maya Makinami"
Lastname. I dont know. Its like trying to see things. But i'll say it anyway. Maybe Sensei and Maya were going to name their unborn child Ami. And that would mean (because she is pregnant at that time) Maya (is) Makin(g) Ami... this is more fun than a theory. Or maybe Ami is a part stripped from Maya's mind? Or it just means nothing.

"Ami (Makinami?)"
Im pretty sure there is a scene where Ami calls Sensei dad, or daddy. And you can't make her call you that as a lustname without breaking the world. Maybe her saying that was a glitch in the world/simulation or a hint about their true relation.

"The stillborn Baby"
There are people out there that go all for the religous stuff (trinity, gods play a role) and think that the stillborn baby might be one of the three gods trying to, i dont know, get born again.
I'd rather (yeah not really because sad, but for story purpose) see the baby as Senseis and Mayas baby with Maya having a misscarriage due to the car crash. And it might implicate Sensei having a grudge (subconsciously) against Maya with how she talked about that stuff in baby finches. Explicitly with her "how baby finches might get revenge on their parents (mothers) (gnarling through their dead bodys) (yeah as she remembered herself, birds lay eggs)" and (i dont remember that correctly) someones entrails? becoming acid? I hope you get what i mean... (Mayas body rejecting their baby, The reason he sees her as a finch? in .14?, really hope im wrong, totally not my thing).

"Kumon'mi/The Town which apparently has two halfes"
So space war huh? No... i guess this is just an excuse for having the world ( almost ) without males.
And a reason to have a barrier at town limits.
Thinking of two halfes and that Sensei might be in Hopes simulation those two halfes could represent Senseis brain. And one half is still damaged (Hence the glitches/Happy scenes/his strange behavior). Or thats the half where his old memories reside. Or its two halfes ruled by two different entities with the darker one ruled by an incarnation of Maya... i guess we'll see. I can see Tojo ramen and its residents playing part in that one too.

"Trinity or
" For a second there, it felt like we were three minutes-lion robots coming together to form one super robot ""
As is said i dont think the whole religion, philosophy, metaphor things in the Happy scenes have much meaning.
With this as maybe one of a few exceptions.
If Maya and Sensei are connected to terminal 23 as users with a third one being unkown or Hope its possible that they are a representation of the trinity. And those are the 3 gods who are one god (The system/simulation) and no real gods at all.
(Self reminder. Found the names of those 3 gods again, which are "The callous, the calm and the concerned one")

"Kaori the queen of spiders and darkness and only one chicken"
First i thought about Kaori as some kind of Hope subordinate. Like if she was a sub ai functioning as a metacrawler search engine. Given how she works about a dozen places and how shes talking, that might still be true.
But with her memoryloss and how she remembers her first memory at all (loud sound/head injury), plus the spiders from baby finches maybe she was in that other car, the not Sensei and Maya, or his brother and sister in law one. There're people who think a young Kaori is the one shadow in baby finches that has that spider hanging from a thread above shadow ami's head. I dont see a resemblence there but who knows. Guys said it was almost confirmed so hmmm.
All in all i do think she might be connected to that stuff. Which leads us to...

"Miku"
I could also see her as a person (a fragment of Sensei or Maya) being involved in that specific car crash.
Which might be a reason why she snaps from loud noises.

"Tsuneyo and Tojo ramen"
Only two things here for now i wonder about.
First:
Is that really her father on the upper floor? Or maybe Maya or Sensei or someone we dont know yet?
The way she discribes him sounds like another person connected to terminal 23.
Second:
I wonder if its not the first, if her father is even still alive or already dead for some time. It just feels like that could be coming to us in a very happy scene.

"Makoto"
So, bluejay. I dont know who or what was exactly responsible for that. Either her father being absent (daddy issues again) or Sensei with the way he treated her, or both, her mother not behaving like a mother but a friend, plus a lot more i guess.
Somewhere before or actual during bluejay, Sensei (i guess a darker part of him) says something about that he might have planted a dark seed into her which would eventually become a sick rose. This might be a reference to the way he treats her
or (with the possibility of Maya having been pregnant ) maybe it was some of his former self shining through and fearing he might got her literally pregnant with the same outcome as for Maya.
After bluejay and Makoto snapping i think there was a scene where Sensei had one of his inner monologues saying that maybe all she wanted was to hear something specific from him. Something showing that he cares for her something that would give her comfort. In the end a reset (Hope) took care of a lot of bluejay and its implications, but not flawlessly.

"Resets and their rules"
This mostly comes from Maya. And she gives those information only hesitantly (thats a rooftop question etc.). Or if she's in the mood or because of Noriko .
So normally the world seems to reset regularly. I guess that has to do with what Maya says about people in Kumon'mi getting a part of their memories erased and the remaining altered. I think of it like take away the details and only leave ideas to them behind and make it so that it makes sense for those people involved.
This is explained by Maya (in: Now more then ever):
Computers have hardrives. „Over time, those harddrives fill up with information a user collects and saves.“
„If a household has one computer and every resident of the house uses it, that storage space will begin to fill up rather quickly.“
„So, in order to make space for new information, old information needs to be deleted.“
„Or reformatted entirely in more severe cases.“
„What you were experiencing in watching those girls adapt to you was a type of reformatting.“
„They were freeing up space in their minds to make room for the new you“
„And unless you do something to ruin them (bluejay), which you likely will because you are horrible, that will be how they remain until a new user comes along.“

When Sensei royally fucked up in bluejay and anything Makoto related before that, Makoto, within the next reset got all the bluejay memories removed from her. Normally, everyone who knew about her strange behavior would have happened something similar to them too... but as we see, not only Sensei remembers her not being well but also her mother. Just this time (and this is about Sensei) people have a chance for a better outcome and not rehappening bluejay at all. Her mother goes into real mom mode and Sensei gives her the needed appreciation and comfort. He is even once totally honest to her (yeah im going after other girls too). Thats one of the reasons that i think hes really trying to be a better person, he just makes that few very tiny baby steps. But i guess we will see some increase in momentum someday.

So i said normal resets. Their might have been some irregular resets in the past. Maybe Sensei tried to kill himself over and over for the first few cycles instantly prompting a reset. Or when he found out about himself or whatever also prompting a reset.
And those even erased and altered his memories to a point where he someday could manage to stay alive/sane.

"Ami, Maya, Niki, Noriko and Sensei"
So i had to put this into yet another spoiler tag because "their past" takes alot of space in the entire story.
But at least it gives me the opportunity for some slight reformatting that wouldn't fit with the rest of the text.

Leaving that one out till i replayed .16 because of the new Ami scenes that seem to mix up what Noriko told us.
This is up to .16p1
Credits to zekemckillip for our conversation about that topic.

So, this includes main events "What could have been", "What is", "What was", Niki, Noriko and Maya events from .15p1 and Ami's "Heaven for Human Blood" from .16p1.
I guess i could really put that into another post itself given how long this might get. But that would be countering the purpose of this post.
I'll try to get this sorted in some way because we do get some "facts" (more to that later) but just not enough to pin things down exactly (but very close) but more in a time range.

Main events:
What could have been (Noriko class introduction):
- Noriko and Sensei last met 3 years ago.
- Noriko admires (first says she loved him but admits that was an exaggeration.) Sensei since she was 6.
- Noriko knows "niece" Ami.
- Maya mentiones timelines. Sensei goes ? to this. Noriko goes: "We'll see about..."
(Noriko seems to have done something in the past that infuriates Maya (and i have an idea what that was). It also implies that Noriko might be aware of Kumon'mi (reset/loop) rules.)

What is:
- Noriko and Sensei have been neighbors (in the old district).
- Sensei says there has to be a good 15 years (age) between him and Noriko. ("Later" we find out that he's 31 making her around ~ 16.)
- Sensei stopped coming over to Niki and Noriko's place after "that thing" (Car accident i guess) happened.
- Sensei and Noriko met after "that thing". Several times even, it seems.
- Niki and Noriko's parents called Sensei after "that thing" to tutor Noriko. (Did they not know what happened?)

What was:
- Niki and Sensei have been a couple for 5 years.
- Niki remembers Ami and an accident.

Noriko events:
Sculpture (Dream Girl):
- Niki and Sensei were a couple.
- Maya and Noriko got tutored by Sensei.
(Noriko seems to be obsessed of Sensei)

Nakayarakawayama:
- Noriko says that all Niki did till she was 18 was drawing doodle anime characters (whatever that is). (This implies Niki became an idol at that time but thats no real fact.)

Semi Constructive Criticism:
- Noriko says that Sensei taught them (her and Maya) about Orwell when they were 10.
(Here Noriko says something like Sensei taught them weird stuff. And i somehow hope that weird in this case means that Orwell is more something meant more for grownups. More on that later.)
- Noriko says that instead what Sensei thinks, Maya might not be so happy if Sensei vanished for good.
- Noriko slips that she could totally tell Sensei things „that happend which actually never happened“ because of his „amnesia“. (This one might be really important, so i'll come back to this.)

New Shoes:
- Noriko says that her and Ami knew for a short period in the past.
- Noriko says she knew Sensei her entire life because they were neighbors.
- Sensei came over to Niki and Noriko's place even before dating Niki.
- Sensei has an inner monologue where he thinks that old Sensei might have hidden (his past) the whole Nikki relationship, Noriko and Maya tutor stuff from Ami (Maybe because of car accident).

Beginnings. Endings. Things in Between:
- Noriko says that Maya is a big part of why she thinks Sensei disapeared the last time.
- Noriko says that she thinks that Maya wants to take Sensei away. Get him to herself and that she cant win over her.
Puhhh okay here it is and i thought i was just seeing things:
- Noriko: „But the second i find out that she’s trying to steal you away from me again, i‘m going to hang her by her intestines off the tallest tree i can find.“
(Important part here of course is the word "again" implying that Sensei and Maya had something going on "romantically".)

Niki events:
Cotton candy:
Joke: Selebus messed up here, because it should haven been 23 Productions
Nothing else so far.

Like it’s Any other Day:
(It seems the car crash happened when Sensei and Niki were still together. I guess at the end of their relationship, even the reason for him breaking up with her, or just silently leaving.)
- Niki says Sensei is 31 (close to what he thought how old he is) which by her saying she's 2 years younger makes her 29.
- Niki says she wasted basically her entire 20’s on him. (This is slightly in conflict with the time period they were a couple, him breaking up when she was max 21, more to that later. It could just mean she mourned their relationship a long time in her 20's or was searching for him in her 20's.)
- Niki says that their 2 year age gap was anoying in highschool.
(So if this refers to Japanese high school it would translate to something like: highschool ages from 14-18. 2 year gap. They share one year together. He‘s 18 shes 16 at that point.)

Maya Events:
What it Means to Be Destroyed:
- Maya says that Noriko has a long history of getting in the way (between her and original Sensei? Competing for his affection?).
- Also Sensei might come into trouble because Noriko cant keep a secret. (This might be a hint i will try to explain later.)
- She also says that SHE kept Noriko away and that it doesn’t concern Sensei.
- Maya admits that Sensei tutored her too.
- Maya says that Sensei disappeared on Noriko before. (Same as Noriko said.)
There is a bit more in this event but thats more about Kumon'mi (resets/loops) mechanics.

Now More Than Ever:
- Maya says that Senseis old life was boring and sad (which one though? Old real life or a past Kumon’mi life?)
Again theres of course more in this event which is about other topics though.

A Place That Can Only Exist in Our Minds:
- Sensei has some statics
- Maya asks him if he sees things (because static).
- Maya asks: „Do you see them when you're with „her (Noriko)“ as well?“ „Shouldn’t that be telling you something?“
Depends if she means he’s or he’s not seeing things (remembering) if he’s with Noriko too.
- Maya: "You might just be… you. …" I leave this in because its generally important with her implicating that new Sensei is in fact old Sensei.
Maya goes ssssssssssss kkkkkkkkkkkkk after that. So someone/thing is interfering here. Angels?

Ok... Sensei and Ami where living together at Ami’s parents home.

The epic conclusion:
So where do i start?
Sensei, Niki, Noriko and it seems Maya have been neighbors in the old district their entire lives to a certain point, with Sensei being the oldest of them. It isn't exactly stated where Maya comes from but she was there. Sensei seems to have visited the Niki/Noriko household a long time in the past and somewhen started a relationship with Niki. It is stated that this relationship lasted for 5 years and that it was a thing when Niki and Sensei went to highschool together.
Though, we're not given when that relationship started and when it ended.
It's likely that Ami was 7 when the car crash happened and that that was the reason for Sensei to break up with Niki (Sensei is 31, Ami,Noriko and Maya are ~15y younger, Ami is 7 when car crash makes Sensei ~22 and Niki ~20 when car crash and split up.)
But given the information we have, that
the relationship was still a thing when they were at highschool and, doing some math, she was ~16 and him ~18 at that time. This gives us a time range from her being ~11 to ~21 with him from ~13 to ~23 for their relationship to happen in. In that range of time, "that thing" (car crash) happens, Sensei breaks up with Niki and leaves the old district. After that however he's asked by Noriko's parants to tutor her (Likely when he's  ~22). He seems to be tutoring Noriko and Maya from that point which is either before them being 10 or starting when they were 10 (Likely started when they both were ~7/8). It's highly possible though that this lasted until 3 years prior now.
(I'll leave this as is so people see where i made changes. Will remove things in the future.)
- So, why doesn't Ami rember all this? Sensei has an inner monologue where he thinks he might have never told her about this stuff. And in "Heaven for Human Blood" Ami comes up with the same idea.
- Why doesn't Niki know about the tutoring and that he came back? I don't know why her parents didn't tell her but Noriko might not have told her because she wanted to leave her out as a rival in love.
So what might have happened back then:
Ami somehow confirms that things might have happened as they seem. But Ami got jealous of how the tutoring seemed to had have a positive impact on Sensei although she still took care of him. She felt like they were slowly growing apart. So ultimately she decides tutoring went different and without Maya involved.
So it seems Sensei tutored Maya and Noriko, he started a "relationship" with Maya and Noriko who fell in love for Sensei too, either accidently or intentionally told someone about it or even threatened them with it for her own advantage. Which is the reason why Maya is pissed off about her. This might even be the reason why he stopped tutoring and left Noriko the last time, 3 years ago, maybe taking Maya with him.
Maya might fear that their past might repeat hence her outbursts about Noriko.
Two things for now though that might still mix stuff up.
- The term timeloops got thrown in, so we even don't know if this all happened in reallife or in one or more Kumon'mi loops.
- And Noriko stated that she could tell Sensei things that happened that actually never happened, questioning the validity of everything she said. But given Maya's reactions, at least a good chunk of the whole story seems to be correct.
I guess this concludes  my theory on that part of the story... and it got totally out of hand.

- Maya says that Senseis old life was boring and sad (which one though? Old real life or a past Kumon’mi life?)
Again theres of course more in this event which is about other topics though.

A Place That Can Only Exist in Our Minds:
- Sensei has some statics
- Maya asks him if he sees things (because static).
- Maya asks: „Do you see them when you're with „her (Noriko)“ as well?“ „Shouldn’t that be telling you something?“
Depends if she means he’s or he’s not seeing things (remembering) if he’s with Noriko too.
- Maya: "You might just be… you. …" I leave this in because its generally important with her implicating that new Sensei is in fact old Sensei.
Maya goes ssssssssssss kkkkkkkkkkkkk after that. So someone/thing is interfering here. Angels?
We also see "loli Maya" for the first time here. Sensei also "scans" Maya and that scan deems her "broken beyond repair" (i guess this is a hint too.).
Ok i got to somehow summarizer this because i have lines and lines of remarks to explain all this.
Maya would even go so far as to "go to town" with Sensei so he might remember things of their past and abandon Noriko. Her way of smoothly (by sensations) trying to make Sensei remember opposed to Norikos brute force appraoch by openly telling him.
- Sensei sees Maya as a bird (finch i guess).
- Maya: „Which really pisses me off by the way since Noriko can apparently tell you EVERYTHING without you hallucinating her as a fucking animal!“
So yeah Maya is mad about how Noriko can use her brute force ways, without Sensei hallucinating like he is with Maya trying to tell him things.
Ah... this event has lots of backdoor information that don't directly relate to the whole Sensei's past with Niki,Noriko, Maya stuff... It's just hard to disassemble it into something sorted and meaningful for this section of the post.

Stop Looking For Answers:
- Maya at least pretends not to know anything about why Sensei saw her as a bird.
- Maya: "But, then again, everything I know about the world has been slowly fading away since winter began." (Because at least Noriko arrived?)
- Maya: "She’s (Noriko) going to chase you off the same way she did the last time." (This will go into summarization)
Again i have to summarize.
- Maya admits that new Sensei "probably" is old Sensei.
- Maya: "Saying “definitely” too soon and then losing you would be the emotional equivalent of dropping my body feet first into a meat grinder."
(Implicating a deeper relationship, her true feelings for him.)

Ami Event:
Heaven for Human Blood:
- Sensei has an inner monologue: "The only thing is that I can’t personally confirm if it’s the same type of tantrum she’d throw when she was really little because her parents didn’t die until she was seven." (So her parents died when she was 7?)
- Ami: "You didn’t meet her (Maya) until I started bringing her home in middle school." (Japanese middle school is from age 12 - 15)
Summarization of a range of dialogue
Ok... Sensei and Ami where living together at Ami’s parents home.
They were initially caring alot for each other (because car crash and it’s implications, while i guess Ami was doing most of the work.) till-
Some time after that Sensei started to get better and even they were still close, Ami wondered why he was getting better without her help (some jealousy here). And if something was hindering them to get even closer. He was coming home later and later.
- Ami says that she doesn’t think this was because he was tutoring (but yeah it was).
- Ami asks why he never brought his tutoring students back home (new district) and Sensei answers that that would have been weird and their parents wouldn’t have been very fond of that.
- Ami says that maybe something happened while Sensei was tutoring and that in the end he gave up on it.
- Ami says that it was maybe because of Noriko or Maya which Sensei denies.
- Ami tells Sensei that he never tutored Maya, at least not that she was aware of. And if he did he must have hidden it from her (which i guess he did).
- Ami goes into jealousy mode again and that everything they went through should mean more than everything someone (Noriko/Maya) just might have made up.
- Ami: "So either everything is fake...or you’ve been hiding something very bad from me for a very long time..." (It’s the second i guess)
- Ami: "Or you’re just misremembering and talked about tutoring Maya on accident!"
First: The scene changes from static backgroud to normal one.
Second: I think this is a point where Ami just decides how to handle all this. And she decides that the Maya tutoring stuff never happened. (And so the static background returns to a normal one.)

The epic conclusion:
So where do i start?
Sensei, Niki, Noriko and it seems Maya have been neighbors in the old district their entire lives to a certain point, with Sensei being the oldest of them. It isn't exactly stated where Maya comes from but she was there. Sensei seems to have visited the Niki/Noriko household a long time in the past and somewhen started a relationship with Niki. It is stated that this relationship lasted for 5 years and that it was a thing when Niki and Sensei went to highschool together. Though, we're not given when that relationship started and when it ended. It's likely that Ami was 7 when the car crash happened and that that was the reason for Sensei to break up with Niki (Sensei is 31, Ami,Noriko and Maya are ~15y younger, Ami is 7 when car crash makes Sensei ~22 and Niki ~20 when car crash and split up.) But given the information we have, that the relationship was still a thing when they were at highschool and, doing some math, she was ~16 and him ~18 at that time. This gives us a time range from her being ~11 to ~21 with him from ~13 to ~23 for their relationship to happen in. In that range of time, "that thing" (car crash) happens, Sensei breaks up with Niki and leaves the old district. After that however he's asked by Noriko's parants to tutor her (Likely when he's ~22). He seems to be tutoring Noriko and Maya from that point which is either before them being 10 or starting when they were 10 (Likely started when they both were ~7/8). It's highly possible though that this lasted until 3 years prior now.
(I'll leave this as is so people see where i made changes. Will remove things in the future.)

- So, why doesn't Ami rember all this? Sensei has an inner monologue where he thinks he might have never told her about this stuff. And in "Heaven for Human Blood" Ami comes up with the same idea.
- Why doesn't Niki know about the tutoring and that he came back? I don't know why her parents didn't tell her but Noriko might not have told her because she wanted to leave her out as a rival in love.

So what might have happened back then:
Ami somehow confirms that things might have happened as they seem. But Ami got jealous of how the tutoring seemed to had have a positive impact on Sensei although she still took care of him. She felt like they were slowly growing apart. So ultimately she decides tutoring went different and without Maya involved.
So it seems Sensei tutored Maya and Noriko, he started a "relationship" with Maya and Noriko who fell in love for Sensei too, either accidently or intentionally told someone about it or even threatened them with it for her own advantage. Which is the reason why Maya is pissed off about her. This might even be the reason why he stopped tutoring and left Noriko the last time, 3 years ago, maybe taking Maya with him.
Maya might fear that their past might repeat hence her outbursts about Noriko.

Two things for now though that might still mix stuff up.
- The term timeloops got thrown in, so we even don't know if this all happened in reallife or in one or more Kumon'mi loops.
- And Noriko stated that she could tell Sensei things that happened that actually never happened, questioning the validity of everything she said. But given Maya's reactions, at least a good chunk of the whole story seems to be correct.

I guess this concludes my theory on that part of the story... and it got totally out of hand.

spoilers.title: Up to .25p1
spoilers.html:
So opposite of just editing everything i already wrote i'm just putting new thoughts here.
Didn't wrote anything for a year. Trying to take every event apart was just to much of an effort and i respect everyone who can remember every event to it's details, which i can not do and will not do, no matter how good the story is.

So i'm going to make an "assumption" about a good part of the story, mainly Senseis's past.

Chances are that Sensei, his brother and Maya (and maybe others) grew up in the upside down house. An orphanage of some kind.
It could also have been in any regular school of some kind, but Sekai wearing a cross gives it some religious wibes and finally gives the upside down house a meaning.
For me, that sets everything in an katholic kind of setting, even explaining all the religious stuff we experience in the game (Mainly that religion and gods are bad/want something from you).

There they all got abused/raped. This could go in hand with the famouse "Why does it have to hurt so much", meaning first time sexual expierence.
While, at least those three got raped/abused, at least Sensei's brother got so twisted that he became used to it and even took over that ill behavior.
Afaik it's mentioned by Sekai/The Teacher/ Ami's Mom the she started a relationship with Sensei's brother (Nozomu).

So we skip ahead a few years were Sensei is free to live on his own and somewhen takes Maya with him. He shares a deep bond with Maya, made by their shared experiences. (He might have also taken over some of the ill behavior he learned in the orphanage, but thats another story. )

Sekai/The teacher and Sensei's brother/Nozomu have a relationship and the result of that is Ami.
Here is where my theory might collapse and that wouldn't be bad, that be totally ok with me.
At Sekai's/Nozomu's grave somewhere in .23 i guess? Sekai appears as a ghost? and comforts Ami.
That wouldn't be a sign of an abusive/bad mother.
So maybe Sekai changed the moment she got Ami. Leaving her abusive/rapist past behind.
But maybe not so much for Nozomu/Sensei's brother?
Here comes the interesting part.

What if Sensei's brother deemed Ami, at a specific age (was it 7 when car crash happened?) to be ready for his special treatment?
Like he thought she was old enough to do to her what he learned to do to others?

Maybe Sensei thought that his brother might do the unspeakable to his own daughter and decided to end it once and for all?
This could then lead to the famouse car crash. Maybe Sensei and Maya planned to kill Sensei's brother by manipulating his car (brakes?) and Sekai was just a colleteral damage in the same car.

After all Sensei couldn't take it anymore mostly because Sekai died too in the car crash and finally jumps from the school roof, where the game starts.

spoilers.title: Maybe Candy
spoilers.html:
So, funny thing, where coincidence can take you.
Someone posts that you need 2000 affection points with Ayane to see a special event and you coincidentally see something looking for the correct event in a girls events.
I thought about it , what i mean, a long time ago already and it could totally mean nothing.
That 2000 points post though got me to remember to look into it again.

But I'm leaving it behind as a hint for those interested. And i'll make it cryptic for now .

Four letters and several names.

Like to see what others might come up with or already came up with.

I guess this post is so burried and very few dare to click a link in a signature, that i can freely write what i "might" have found out (gotta scratch that itch).
And if someone reads this, i can watch the virus spread

Given all the cryptics we have in the game, ceasar zypher, hexdec, i guess binary was a thing and who knows what else, starting with amiokay i tried tho find more clues in names.
Maya Makinami seemed already to be a hint to something. In a theory where Maya might be Ami's true mother, with Sensei as the father, it would make sense that Maya (is/was) makin' Ami.
But i couldn't find any more names with a meaning, that is, until recently.
So is, for those who know, Amiokay just Am i Okay or Ami Okay?
I think it might be neither of those.
Maybe everything revoles around Maya - M A Y A.
I have i theory and i stated that way above in this post, that girls in Kumon'mi might be split apart or maybe copies of, either Senseis and or Maya's and who knows who else's mind.
So i started looking for Maya's and Sensei's in other girls and i think i found some (Maya's).

Most important and what made me think i might be right:
Yumi Yamaguchi.
As i said it's about M A Y A.
So: Yumi Guchi Maya. Or Maya Guchi.
While there might be also a translation for Maya in japenese (i guess it was something like love or maybe love interest) Guchi "could" be translated as complaining. And i guess that would be a good definition of Yumis character. Always complaining of how shitty her life is or how Sensei treats her.
That in the end, as a part of Maya would make her Maya's complaining side of her character.

But there are more.

Ayane Amamiya
Amamiya -> Only thing that came up yet -> I am Maya.
So is Ayane the real Maya? A girl we have yet to see (Melon vendor)?
Or is she another fragment, with the letters IAM/MIA/AMI/MAI to make sense?

Makoto Miyamura
Miyamura -> Miru or Muri Maya. Or other combinations.
So this is rather tough. Miru would be to look after someone, like medically caring. Or caring in general which "could" suit Makoto as she's always looking after Sensei to help him, as the class president. Maybe also in another way? A Maya that looked after Seinsei/Cared for him?
Muri seems to be generally about impossible things. Or meaning unreasonable. Makoto the unreasonable Maya? Don't know.

Miku Maruyama
Maruyama -> Maru or Mura Maya? Whatever it is i can't come up with a meaningful answer. Village, circle, complete maybe someting i didn't find out yet.
My guess would be to find some word meaning unsteady, energetic or jittery.

Futaba Fukuyama
Fukuyama ->Fuku Maya? Fuku can mean happy among a ton of other things i guess (vice/clothes/happy). While kufu on ther other hand means things like fear, terror, horror and so on. Could make her, amongst others, the happy or scared Maya.

Noriko Nakayama

alex2011 said:
It isn't a stretch, it should be obvious not to grind too much after that because it happened before. Breaking the promise is only the in universe explanation, the technical explanation is too much grinding because you can ONLY break your promise to Rin by grinding too far. That is now and always has been the issue, grinding too far causes it, so it should set the player up to learn from their mistake and not do it again, which it does to most people, including myself. That only counts as bad game design to you, it does not generally speaking.

There is a colossal gap between having consequences that can't be triggered and having consequences that can be as well. What you are suggesting would result in the former, not the latter. It would eliminate the threat of consequences because the player would be unable to do anything to trigger said consequences. As it is now, not everything in the game has a set of options tied to a consequence and those consequences would be the only ones that remain if the events were made to be required. Missing an opportunity to do something means it is gone forever unless it repeats some time in the future, that is the consequence emulated by the game in this case. Too much time passed in universe and the opportunity to do whatever the event would have allowed with it.

Rin has only been brought up in this exchange as an example, she is not the subject of the exchange. Rin's scenario sets the rule for general purposes, not just for her. What applies to one applies to all in practice. If you're not supposed to grind too much in her case, you're not supposed to in any case. Keeping the promise specifically means not grinding too much in technical terms. As I said before, the only way to set up the trigger for the bad outcome is to grind Chika too far, so that makes grinding too much the cause of Rin's bad outcome in that scenario. After having encountered that, it should then be obvious that it could come up later because rarely, if ever, do games do things only once and never again.

robot

Which might be a reason why she snaps from loud noises.

Is that really her father on the upper floor? Or maybe Maya or Sensei or someone we dont know yet?

or (with the possibility Maya having been pregnant ) maybe it was some of his former self shining through and fearing he might got her literally pregnant with the same outcome as for Maya.

Something showing that he cares for her something that would give her comfort. In the end a reset (Hope) took care of a lot of bluejay and its implications, but not flawlessly.

.
So normally the world seems to reset regularly. I guess that has to do with what Maya says about people in Kumon'mi getting a part of their memories erased and the remaining altered. I think of it like take away the details and only leave ideas to them behind and make it so that it makes sense for those people involved.

And those even erased and altered his memories to a point where he someday could manage to stay alive/sane.
"Maya, Sensei, Niki and Noriko"
Leaving that one out till i replayed .16 because of the new Ami scenes that seem to mix up what Noriko told us.
"Upside down house"
Need to rewatch the movie night scene. will come back.

So stay tuned.
Ill be back (at this).

Fascinating theories. In my opinion it is entirely too early to give credence to any kind of attempt to piece together the numerous puzzle pieces we have been given, especially since there are supposedly 4 different "routes" (depending on how you count) and we're still not even close to done with the first one. However, you have shone a new light at some of those pieces in my mind, specifically the idea of a trinity and how it may not be the main, or at least one of the major focuses of the "hidden" plot(s).
What's your opinion/ideas on USER2? They quite clearly influenced the world/Sensei's perception of the world in multiple instances, and supposedly they are the ones connected to/with wires (if my notes aren't incorrect).

.

Fascinating theories. In my opinion it is entirely too early to give credence to any kind of attempt to piece together the numerous puzzle pieces we have been given, especially since there are supposedly 4 different "routes" (depending on how you count) and we're still not even close to done with the first one. However, you have shone a new light at some of those pieces in my mind, specifically the idea of a trinity and how it may not be the main, or at least one of the major focuses of the "hidden" plot(s).
What's your opinion/ideas on USER2? They quite clearly influenced the world/Sensei's perception of the world in multiple instances, and supposedly they are the ones connected to/with wires (if my notes aren't incorrect).

Furthermore, because of the more gentle actions of USER2, that gives me reason to believe USER2 is old Sensei, the one from before the events of the game. That's my current theory on the USER situation and what is happening as far as weird moments in the story, anyway.

Alright, I have to join in. I'm caught up to .15 pt2, which is as far as I will play until .16 pt1 is free. I really just wanted to say that I think there are answers, or maybe just questions, but something that is being missed with There is Nothing. First off, everyone keeps talking about 3 gods and users and trinity, that's great, but there are 4 users, technically 5. If you type in USER4 it says that it is reserved, not that it is invalid, which means it is a user. Similarly HOPE triggers HE11, and isn't considered and invalid username anyway, although I'm not sure if it should be considered an actual USER or not. Either way that means there is USER1(Offline), USER2(Under maintenance, maybe since HE10, maybe just because we're in a reset event?), USER3(Refusing connection), and USER4(Reserved). I'm not sure what I take away from all this though, because at first I really thought that the USERs were maybe ID, Ego, and Superego. Obviously that can't be right since there is no 4th component to personality/persona, so I'm thinking maybe the Gods theory could be right, as some events to mention becoming/creating a new god. Also, someone said recently that the IP address isn't a real IP address, and while this is true, it is VERY close to a real IPv6 address(only the x994 part invalidates it, the 2 sections that are 5b7:489 can be assumed to have leading zeroes that were shortened out, which is valid in IPv6), and I wonder if that is significant. Anyway, I'm fresh off actually seeing all the events for the first time and I need to go back and rewatch most of the beginning events especially, with now knowing about as much as I can at this point, but I wanted to share some stuff I hadn't seen anyone mention, incase it sparked something for your guys.

Edit: added additional explanation to IP bit for clarification incase anyone isn't familiar with IPv6

I don't think the ID, Ego, and Superego are individual users. They are not just the components of persona, but also stages of development -- we're born as simply ID, the Ego forms when we need to start learning to satisfy our urges in ways that do not get us in trouble, and finally the Superego forms as society's moral norms begin to influence our thoughts, rather than just our actions.

posts.content_html_raw:
This is my current theory for the game:

My current theory, is that it's some form of experiment by a secret organisation. I mainly think the experiment could either be either to create changes in the personality in an individual (In this case Sensei) and to control his mind; or to combat the effects of a mental illness, likely schizophrenia, in order to try and save Sensei from that very condition. Of course, the setting of this experiment is taking place in an alternate reality, with both Sensei and all of the other characters connected to it, likely by different machines which keep their consciousness within this reality. This would also explain the constant references to wires, as all of them could be connected to the machines which keep them trapped in there. An additional point, it would also explain why the girls can't get pregnant. This is because while their minds are connected in this alternate reality, their physical bodies are not.
I've heard that people think Sensei has some form of mental illness, such as schizophrenia, but maybe the organisation is actually attempting to cure it or else cause it. Or maybe they want to develop mind control techniques, in an alternative reality setting which they can simply carry on resetting the world on an unaware person for the sake of convenience. If he were to be suffering from some form of personality disorder, it's safe to assume those personalities could be entirely different from one another, which seeing as current Sensei is nothing like old Sensei, and there is potentially a next Sensei when the current Sensei is lost, it would explain why they are so different. Each personality would then progressively become more evil, as it can be assumed that his mental illness is becoming worse and less stable (Judging from the happy events and world resets). Seemingly the worst that the old sensei did was give detention to the students, especially Yumi, and obviously this sensei has done far worse than that.
It would also explain why when Sensei does lose control, such as when he kisses Yumi and when he has thoughts of killing people, it is a more evil and less controlled version of himself. He has no memories of these events, because in his mind he was another person, another personality in which he has no control over.
As well as that, it explains why Maya is desperate for the older Sensei to come back. The people are all trapped within this alternate reality, potentially a new version of Sensei could destroy both himself and the world. The current Sensei is a lot darker than the old Sensei, which is why she both mistrusts him, and partially blames him for what's happened. Yet she does understand it isn't entirely his fault, she knows it is her responsibility to somehow fix the impossible.

Next, the organisation may be good or evil, and either can greatly affect the rest of the theory.

If the organisation is good and they are trying to cure Sensei of whatever illness he has, then possibly when Maya prays during a world reset, her thoughts directly travel to the workers in the organisation, they listen to her warning about the world breaking and reset it, ensuring that both the world and Sensei are safe. She has stated multiple times she does not believe in god, and yet she prays anyway and her prayers are answered to reset the world. This could indicate that it is people who are controlling the reset, and not a 'god'. But of course, this causes malfunctions and Sensei temporarily loses his mind as they are not yet able to stop or cure whatever mental illness he has. Whenever Sensei's personality changes, this could be simply the schizophrenia taking control and attempting to destroy either Sensei's remaining sanity or the world. Moreover, the different 'Users' may be various workers in the organisation taking direct control of the situation, in order to save Sensei. The evil 'God' or whatever he is that is referenced quite a few times, could be a metaphor for the root cause of his mental illness. It could be a symbolisation for trauma, or the schizophrenia that is keeping him in this state. And of course, this evil god makes his life hell inside this alternate reality, because it is the very reason that he is there in the first place. So in a way, Sensei is himself that being, and he is slowly destroying himself. Which is why if the organisation is good, they are doing this experiment to save him.

If the organisation are mostly evil, then I think they are attempting to control Sensei and damage him beyond repair, or else develop a mind control technique which they could then use on people in the real world. And of course seeing as this is experimental technology, the alternate reality breaks because they can't fully control it. Maya can be assumed to be a 'good guy' and here to try and save Sensei, but she has to ensure that Sensei does not understand what is happening or he would truly lose his mind, and her resetting the world is simply buying time until she can find a more permanent solution to the entire situation. Maybe she knows someone inside the organisation that is on her side, and they implement the reset for her, but of course seeing as they don't have full control over the experiment by themselves this would explain why each reset can be very different from the last. Alternatively, the organisation could simply be creating the resets themselves until they have completed their objectives, which is to truly control the mind of another person (Sensei), or to create something else entirely with his consciousness. In any case, I think the latest characters will have a very large part to play in relation to this part of the theory being correct.

But with writing all of this, I have not yet completed the most recent updates, and my thinking may be massively different in the future. This is just the general picture of what I think could be happening

Yeah this is the vibe I'm getting too, except that there are things like... well lets leave it at Bluejay and everything that happens surrounding that. I mean, Noriko has said as young as 3 he was around her, but it has been implied maybe since birth. He dated Niki for 5 years, and he started tutoring Maya and Noriko at age 6, and continued until at least age 10, when he taught them about Orwell. A couple issues with that, first being that that makes all of those events only about 5 years ago, but Ami has been living with him pretty much forever. Secondly, Niki became a pop star after Sensei, but around 18, which would mean about 11 years ago. This is MUCH more consistent with when it is implied Ami would have started living with Sensei, but would mean Sensie disappeared when Noriko was like 7, being REALLY generous with her age and pretending all the girls are 18+, or 5000 year old wizards, however most likely she would have been younger than that. Anyway, only reason I bring this up, is that either Selebus maybe needs to look at how the game has evolved due to stretch goals on Patreon and double check the cohesiveness of his story, OR these inconsistencies aren't inconsistencies, and they're stand-ins for various psychological issues, so there can be inconsistencies, like going to the beach last summer, except that they wouldn't have been in his class then, except they were because reset. I dunno... it's a lot to try to consider, and I can't wait for more.

vanbummel said:
After playing 16p1 I really hope there is more comeuppance for the way Sensei has been treating Miku. Personality wise she is one of my favorite characters and I wanted Sensei to get closer to her, but every h-scene so far (if you can call them that) has been borderline assault, and it doesn't seem like sensei is taking it seriously at all.

After the forced kiss with Yumi, Yumi frequently calls sensei out (as she should) and sensei appears to genuinely feel bad about it (as he should) even though he wasn't really in control of his actions. I think every h-scene with Miku has been worse than the forced kiss, but sensei doesn't seem to feel bad about it at all, and when Miku is reduced to crying, begging sensei to stop touching her, or leaving the room to get away, he just thinks "that sucks, guess I'll have to try even harder to get her to do those things she repeatedly says she doesn't want to do."

IIRC, the plan is for a dark ending to the game before better endings are possible. I hope the treatment of Miku partially contributes to this. She's one of the most innocent girls in the game, and thus far sensei has been remorselessly treating her like crap every time he tries to make a move on her.
Click to expand...
He's not taking it seriously, if he was, he wouldn't be going after every girl in his class just to get laid by all of them. As for that borderline assault part, literally the only time he has actively forced himself on a girl, and this wasn't by his own will, was the Yumi forced kiss and Miku's one event. All others were with the girl's consent or even actively requested or started by the girl.

Yumi's been calling him out since day one, the forced kiss simply gave her more ammo. He does feel bad in this case, and I honestly think this case is warranted that he should not, because he himself was forced to do it. He did not have control of himself and could not have prevented the kiss, so there is no reason to be sorry. If he had forced the kiss under his own power, then I would agree. Player Sensei really jumped the gun with Miku and tried to rush her into accepting him sexually, unlike his previous attempts with other girls. In this case, he was in the wrong and it was definitely worse in terms of morality. However, this only applies to the latest event where he does something. Of course he doesn't feel bad, it was all a part of his plan, only the Yumi kiss was not.

As for the dark route, they will likely all be part of it in the way you mentioned.

PrimeGuy said:
Sensei is absolutely more aggressive with Miku than he should be, and it makes him a bad person. However, I do want to point out that the reason Miku keeps giving for saying no, isn't that she doesn't want to. It's because she doesn't want to hurt Makoto. I think this is the reason Sensei's behaviour is different than it is with Yumi. If Miku claimed to not want the attention at all, I think that he'd act differently. He's under the impression Miku does want the attention, she's just afraid of consequences to her friendship and friend.
Click to expand...
Especially in the later events, he really jumped the gun with her and it almost seems like he's losing his patience, which could very well spell an end to his plan entirely if he isn't careful. It doesn't help that she is using Makoto as her reason, but when a girl says no, you drop it, it doesn't matter why they said no. I fully believe the latest Miku events would not have played out like they did without the Makoto reason for her denials. That is not to say this is her fault, it isn't.

vanbummel said:
That's a good point, and the reason I qualified it as borderline assault. But really that just goes to show how badly Sensei's views are warped and how manipulative his behavior has been with Miku. She knows almost nothing of sex and at least in the early parts of the game I don't think she's sexually interested in Sensei or anyone. Sensei convinces himself that she wants him by either:
  1. Just repeatedly telling her she wants to have sex with him, even when she clearly says she doesn't
  2. Touching her in ways she asked him not to and then using involuntary responses (moaning, orgasm, etc) to convince himself that she had wanted to be touched like that from the start, even when she said she didn't
By the end of 16p1 it seems clear that she is at least somewhat sexually interested in Sensei, but doesn't want to hurt Makoto...but she only got to that point by being repeatedly groped against her wishes, and that's pretty messed up.
Click to expand...
I mean, granted the lack of other men and any interest in girls would also eventually drive her toward player Sensei, but yeah, he does try to convince himself, and her, that his advances are being answered positively and that she does desire him, which is likely what led to him jumping the gun with the later events in combination with Miku's reason for not accepting.

PrimeGuy said:
I think the "waking up sensei" event is also a big part of why Sensei is able to justify his behaviour to himself. Or at least, the effect it had on Miku.
Click to expand...
Indeed

Either way, that means that Noriko was 15 when the school year started, and if that was in April, she's now 16, or the school year started in the fall, which seems to be what is implied, and so she's still 15, making it roughly 5-6 years after Sensei had her and Maya start reading Orwell.

So I tried to break this into parts and answer, but my thoughts don't come out coherent, because this is all interlocked. So the crux of it is that in What Was Noriko says she would feel bad hiding Sensei from Niki, so I find it REALLY hard to believe that for 5 years, a younger Noriko just left her sister in the dark about Sensei while being tutored by him. I sill say that this does make for a 13 year timeline that actually really works for the Niki/Noriko aspect of the story, but the biggest issue is that there has to be a bigger gap the 3 years since the accident, unless I'm just really misreading everything about the Ami/Ayane/Maya/Sensei dynamic. They don't act like Ami has only been living with Sensei for 3 years, and it states explicitly that Ami doesn't remember ever really seeing Noriko, except a vague recollection of a play date when she was younger. However, this can be attributed to Ami's bad memory around the time of the accident.

Also, Niki doesn't act like her and Sensei broke up 8 years ago, hell, she says she wasted MOST of her 20's on him, but if they dated when she was in highschool, which she says they did, then they broke up with her no older than 23 at the extreme, and more likely something like 21, neither of which could be considered most of your 20's. Now she could also be talking about the era of depression/sadness she experienced after the break up, but therein lies another issue, she says she couldn't be mad at him because he just went through something tragic. I really think the accident happened 8 years ago, and Noriko was tutored before the accident while Sensei and Niki were dating. Then he broke up with Niki when the accident happened, but still had his apartment next door. Then, 3 years ago, something else happened and he moved into his current house, or nothing happened and he just didn't tell them and he moved. My theory here, though, is something did happen, but it wasn't bad. I think Sensei started dating Maya when she was in Junior High. I think both Maya and Noriko liked Sensei, and they both know that they both liked him, and he started a relationship with Maya, and moved. Then I think something happened, maybe he was caught and fired because Maya became his student? Maybe, as others have theorized, something happened with Maya, possibly a miscarriage. But I think he dated Maya for about 3 years, something happened, and he tried to kill himself, maybe even by jumping off the school roof. I think this is why Selebus insists that Sensei is bad, because let's face it, a 28 year old getting into a relationship with a 12/13 year old is just... well, let's leave it at I don't think there is any culture where that is acceptable. This is of course, above and beyond what he's been doing in LiL up to this point, which is also highly questionable, but obviously wouldn't have been quite as bad.

On a side note, Selebus has, for sure, made one mistake, and I don't know if it is intentional or not, but the Japanese school year starts in April, and summer break is the first break of the year, not the end of the school year like in the U.S. so it wouldn't be weird at all for them to have been in his class during the last summer break, and thus had the beach trip. Still, I don't know if this mistake was intentional, since I'm sure most of the players of LiL wouldn't know this, so maybe he's trying to make it relatable, and maybe he's just trying to sneak one past everyone, and there is a deeper meaning to the students acting more like they're on a U.S. style school system. Food for thought definitely.

So, wild theory time. One possibility for the crash happened 3 years ago, and Ami just used to visit his apartment in Old Town, is that maybe after 5 years of dating Niki, Sensei's parents died, since they don't seem to be in the game. This could have been a tragic loss that wasn't the accident but still messed Sensei up. He then moves out of his childhood home, and gets an apartment in the old district and Niki's parents don't tell her but they do encourage him to start tutoring Noriko as a way to try to help him get through his loss. This actually makes sense, because they might have felt it best that Niki not be around him, potentially living with him, and wanting to marry him, etc., because he was emotionally unstable, however if he was just a tutor to their younger daughter, then they could still keep in touch with him, and Noriko was just being tutored, he wasn't her primary teacher, and it's not like Noriko was going to marry someone 15 years older than her. But then after 5 years of tutoring, his brother and sister-in-law die in a car crash, and he disappears, maybe even moving into their old house to take over raising Ami because she has nobody else. I can take this one step crazier and say, maybe his brother and his wife were also bringing Ami over a bunch to give Sensei another reason to keep going after their parents died, maybe Sensei started an affair with Sekai(his sister-in-law) during this time, then the accident happened and that's why Sensei was just as affected as Ami. Most of this is fall back theory, and I don't believe it as much as what I said above to BlackDays, but I think it's all within the realm of possibility.

Finally, some stuff that the game supports and contradicts at the same time. First and foremost is that this is all a psychological breakdown of Sensei's and nothing is real. Obviously that line is all over the game, but it could be true if Sensei has had a major psyche break and is in a padded room. This could be the room with clocks, which also has Sensei in an aquarium, which could indicate that he is contained/locked up. In that case, this could all be a mix of memories and hallucinations all of which are just him being crazy as all hell. The only problem I really have with this theory is that it doesn't explain at all what caused the break, and maybe Selebus just hasn't gotten there yet, and that will be the big reveal, and we'll all love it, but I prefer to think that, like any good puzzle, we have the pieces to at least construct the border/outline of this puzzle, and so while we don't have the whole picture, we should be able to start figuring out what it is, and my other theories support that way more. That said, this is easily the best explanation for the time loops that I've got, because everything else is either Religious/Sci-fi and/or Aliens, and I think that Selebus is purposely trying to tell us it isn't any of those things by having: the 3 god's origin stories(well 2 so far, but I expect a third, probably in chapter 3); and the space war, which is so over the top as to make the idea of advanced technology and aliens seem comical.

Alright, that is really long, and I have way too much ADHD for it to make sense, so please forgive me if you made it this far, because this took like 5 hours, and I'm sure it makes little sense.

spoilers.title: Contradictions
spoilers.html: Finally, some stuff that the game supports and contradicts at the same time. First and foremost is that this is all a psychological breakdown of Sensei's and nothing is real. Obviously that line is all over the game, but it could be true if Sensei has had a major psyche break and is in a padded room. This could be the room with clocks, which also has Sensei in an aquarium, which could indicate that he is contained/locked up. In that case, this could all be a mix of memories and hallucinations all of which are just him being crazy as all hell. The only problem I really have with this theory is that it doesn't explain at all what caused the break, and maybe Selebus just hasn't gotten there yet, and that will be the big reveal, and we'll all love it, but I prefer to think that, like any good puzzle, we have the pieces to at least construct the border/outline of this puzzle, and so while we don't have the whole picture, we should be able to start figuring out what it is, and my other theories support that way more. That said, this is easily the best explanation for the time loops that I've got, because everything else is either Religious/Sci-fi and/or Aliens, and I think that Selebus is purposely trying to tell us it isn't any of those things by having: the 3 god's origin stories(well 2 so far, but I expect a third, probably in chapter 3); and the space war, which is so over the top as to make the idea of advanced technology and aliens seem comical.

This is of course, above and beyond what he's been doing in LiL up to this point, which is also highly questionable, but obviously wouldn't have been quite as bad.

On a side note, Selebus has, for sure, made one mistake, and I don't know if it is intentional or not, but the Japanese school year starts in April, and summer break is the first break of the year, not the end of the school year like in the U.S. so it wouldn't be weird at all for them to have been in his class during the last summer break, and thus had the beach trip. So, wild theory time. One possibility for the crash happened 3 years ago, and Ami just used to visit his apartment in Old Town, is that maybe after 5 years of dating Niki, Sensei's parents died, since they don't seem to be in the game. This could have been a tragic loss that wasn't the accident but still messed Sensei up. He then moves out of his childhood home, and gets an apartment in the old district and Niki's parents don't tell her but they do encourage him to start tutoring Noriko as a way to try to help him get through his loss. This actually makes sense, because they might have felt it best that Niki not be around him, potentially living with him, and wanting to marry him, etc., because he was emotionally unstable, however if he was just a tutor to their younger daughter, then they could still keep in touch with him, and Noriko was just being tutored, he wasn't her primary teacher, and it's not like Noriko was going to marry someone 15 years older than her. Most of this is fall back theory, and I don't believe it as much as what I said above to BlackDays, but I think it's all within the realm of possibility.

This could be the room with clocks, which also has Sensei in an aquarium, which could indicate that he is contained/locked up. In that case, this could all be a mix of memories and hallucinations all of which are just him being crazy as all hell. The only problem I really have with this theory is that it doesn't explain at all what caused the break, and maybe Selebus just hasn't gotten there yet, and that will be the big reveal, and we'll all love it, but I prefer to think that, like any good puzzle, we have the pieces to at least construct the border/outline of this puzzle, and so while we don't have the whole picture, we should be able to start figuring out what it is, and my other theories support that way more. Alright, that is really long, and I have way too much ADHD for it to make sense, so please forgive me if you made it this far, because this took like 5 hours, and I'm sure it makes little sense.

spoilers.title: Contradictions
spoilers.html: Finally, some stuff that the game supports and contradicts at the same time. First and foremost is that this is all a psychological breakdown of Sensei's and nothing is real. Obviously that line is all over the game, but it could be true if Sensei has had a major psyche break and is in a padded room. This could be the room with clocks, which also has Sensei in an aquarium, which could indicate that he is contained/locked up. In that case, this could all be a mix of memories and hallucinations all of which are just him being crazy as all hell. The only problem I really have with this theory is that it doesn't explain at all what caused the break, and maybe Selebus just hasn't gotten there yet, and that will be the big reveal, and we'll all love it, but I prefer to think that, like any good puzzle, we have the pieces to at least construct the border/outline of this puzzle, and so while we don't have the whole picture, we should be able to start figuring out what it is, and my other theories support that way more. That said, this is easily the best explanation for the time loops that I've got, because everything else is either Religious/Sci-fi and/or Aliens, and I think that Selebus is purposely trying to tell us it isn't any of those things by having: the 3 god's origin stories(well 2 so far, but I expect a third, probably in chapter 3); and the space war, which is so over the top as to make the idea of advanced technology and aliens seem comical.
